question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 19 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused the spike in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at the change point, causing a sudden increase in request volume.
The increased request volume led to higher latency as the system struggled to handle the load.
The error rate rose due to the system being overwhelmed by the sudden surge in traffic.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of auth v4.9 may have introduced a latency issue.
why_chain: The deployment of auth v4.9 occurred 251 minutes before the change point.
The system's performance degraded after the deployment, leading to increased latency.
The increased latency contributed to the overall system performance degradation.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v1.1 caused the change.
ruled_out.reason: The catalog v1.1 deployment was a routine release and occurred 163 minutes before the change point.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out caused the change.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out occurred 20 minutes after the change point.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 284 ms (+107%), with a change point at 2026-03-19T03:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1267 per 5 min before, 4623 per 5 min after, +265%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.81% after, +100%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 03:30 UTC (ap-south; 127 min before the change; record R015)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R016)
Deployed auth v4.9 to ap-south (auth, ap-south; 251 min before the change; record R013)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R017)
Deployed catalog v1.1 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 163 min before the change; record R014)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (127 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Roll back the auth v4.9 deployment to revert the potential performance degradation.
Implement a traffic management system to handle sudden spikes in traffic during marketing campaigns.
Optimize the autoscaler to better handle sudden traffic spikes.
